evidence.claim: Kishida said he personally had no links to the former Unification Church to the best of his knowledge, told ministerial candidates to examine any connections, and said he appointed only those who agreed to review the ties.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said he personally had no links to the former Unification Church to the best of his knowledge, told ministerial candidates to examine any connections, and said he appointed only those who agreed to review the ties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO transcript with direct contemporaneous statements by the prime minister.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Kishida public statement and cabinet-management instruction; the truth of the personal no-links claim remains unverified within this source.
contrary_evidence: Later reporting showed some newly appointed ministers still had church links, which undercuts the claim that vetting was fully effective.

evidence.claim: Kishida ordered an investigation into the Unification Church under the Religious Corporations Act, apologized that many LDP members' ties undermined public trust, and said the government would clarify the situation and protect victims.
evidence.title: Japan PM orders probe into Unification Church links to ruling party members
evidence.excerpt: Kishida ordered an investigation into the Unification Church under the Religious Corporations Act, apologized that many LDP members' ties undermined public trust, and said the government would clarify the situation and protect victims.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraphs and quoted Kishida remarks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with direct quotation and specific administrative action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Kishida action after public notice of the scandal and its fallout.
contrary_evidence: The report also shows the controversy remained broad and unresolved within the ruling party.

evidence.claim: Kishida accepted criticism that his explanation for the state funeral was insufficient and said he would provide a thorough explanation, while public opposition was tied in part to church-link revelations.
evidence.title: Japan PM defends decision on state funeral for Abe
evidence.excerpt: Kishida accepted criticism that his explanation for the state funeral was insufficient and said he would provide a thorough explanation, while public opposition was tied in part to church-link revelations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with Kishida's own admission that the explanation was insufficient.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a direct public-correction episode by Kishida, but it concerns policy justification more than financial honesty or private gain.
contrary_evidence: The issue is indirect to personal integrity and does not itself demonstrate self-dealing or deliberate lying.

evidence.claim: Kishida said he met people harmed by the former Unification Church, instructed officials to create a new law with the greatest regulation possible under constitutional limits, and set up a government-wide team to help victims use the new system.
evidence.title: Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida
evidence.excerpt: Kishida said he met people harmed by the former Unification Church, instructed officials to create a new law with the greatest regulation possible under constitutional limits, and set up a government-wide team to help victims use the new system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO transcript with concrete remedial instructions and implementation planning.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Kishida response after notice of harm, using executive and legislative authority to create remedy.
contrary_evidence: This is reactive remediation, not proof that earlier party vetting or disclosure was adequate.

unresolved_gaps: Stronger direct evidence of Kishida's personal control over police, prosecutors, and protective institutions before and after the Abe assassination.
More evidence that the church-scandal and protest responses reduced actual harm rather than only improving the public narrative.
More independent evidence that the 2022 growth/distribution package actually changed household welfare or investment outcomes rather than only announcing them.
Better separation of Kishida's policy effect from BOJ policy, exchange-rate moves, and imported inflation shocks.
Direct year-end outcome evidence for child, fertility, and social-service gains attributable to the 2022 package.
More subgroup evidence on single-parent households, disabled people, housing insecurity, and food insecurity.
Direct, traceable evidence of Kishida's own assets, private interests, donor links, or personal self-enrichment is missing.
Independent corroboration of the personal claim that Kishida had no links to the former Unification Church and that his vetting instructions were fully followed.
More independent evidence on whether the 2022 startup, digital, and green-growth agenda actually produced measurable execution, not just planning.
Clearer separation of Kishida's own execution from external shocks and inherited macro conditions when judging the economic package and wage trajectory.
